source.citation: Koga A, Bai X, Jia Y, Liu J (2025). Lower limb biomechanical differences between jumps with different number of rotations in youth figure skaters. Front Bioeng Biotechnol 13:1606817. doi:10.3389/fbioe.2025.1606817 (PMC12434041, CC BY). Table 2, row 'Flight time', column 'Double axel'.
source.notes: Double axel (2.5 rotations), n = 3: three of the eleven skaters; the paper calls this subgroup purely descriptive and exploratory (section 5), so it is weaker evidence than the other two. Open access; read in the full text (PMC12434041), so primary outright. 11 youth skaters (8 F, 3 M), age 12 +/- 4.29 years, 146.82 +/- 17.71 cm, 37.02 +/- 14.47 kg, regional or national level, all taking off from the left foot and turning counterclockwise. Two high-speed cameras at 100 Hz, 3D by DLT, digitised by hand in SIMI Motion. Flight phase (Table 1): 'From the toe-off to initial ground contact on landing foot'. Each jump skated three times; the paper does not say which trials were analysed or whether falls were excluded. Table 2 gives no unit for time; the Discussion (section 4.1) reads it as seconds. Section 3.1's sentence that the waltz jump flies longer than the single axel contradicts Table 2 (0.36 vs 0.40 s); the table is used. u_m is the reported SD. One-sided (fidelity-gate section 4.3 O5): the model has no effort input, so the case asks only that the model can fly at least this long. skater is the cohort's mean body. Script: test/entries.test.ts's axel entry (written before this case, so no input was chosen for it), its stick mirror baked in by test/axel-case-scripts.ts, which also checks it; only the takeoff whip differs between the three Koga cases, and air time does not depend on it. NOTED, NOT ACTED ON (2026-11-15): on this body the model's clean takeoff flies 0.725 s at vz 3.575 m/s, because jumpImpulse is scaled by sqrt(55 / mass) (profile.ts; open-constants section 2, L2). The same table gives take-off vertical velocity (m/s) waltz 1.77 +/- 0.46, single axel 2.24 +/- 0.42, double axel 2.73 +/- 0.31. A one-sided case cannot see a model that flies too long, and the gate has no vz observable; both are the owner's gate decisions. On responsive, 2026-11-15, the script skates an LFO takeoff into an axel, 2.45 rev, clean, standing.
